subject: API returning 429 constantly on Free plan

conversation.text: We're getting HTTP 429 from /v1/widgets after only a minute of light usage. Is something broken on your side?

Nothing is broken. The Free plan is capped at 60 requests per minute per API key. Once you cross it we return 429 with a Retry-After header telling you how many seconds to wait. Check the X-RateLimit-Remaining header on every response to see how close you are before you get cut off.
Is the limit per key or per account?
Per API key. Creating a second key does not give you more total throughput on Free — the account ceiling is still 60 req/min shared across keys.

resolution: Explained Free plan limit of 60 requests/minute per API key, shared across keys at account level. Customer upgraded to Pro.

subject: Rate limit seems lower than advertised on Pro

conversation.text: We upgraded to Pro expecting more headroom but still see 429s during our nightly batch.

Pro is 600 requests per minute per API key. Your batch job is bursting to roughly 900 req/min for short windows. The limiter uses a fixed one-minute window, not a rolling average, so a burst at the start of a window will exhaust the quota immediately.
Any way to smooth that out?
Spread the batch with a small delay between calls, and honour Retry-After rather than retrying immediately. Retrying without backoff is counted against the same window and makes it worse.

resolution: Clarified Pro limit is 600 requests/minute per key with a fixed one-minute window. Advised client-side throttling and honouring Retry-After.

subject: Need higher throughput for data migration

conversation.text: We are migrating 40 million records and need to know our ceiling.

Enterprise accounts are provisioned at 6000 requests per minute per API key by default. For one-off migrations we can raise it temporarily — we have lifted customers to 20000 req/min for a scheduled window. Give us 5 business days notice and the window you need.

resolution: Enterprise default is 6000 requests/minute per key. Temporary uplift to 20000 req/min available with 5 business days notice.

subject: Refund still not showing on my card

conversation.text: You confirmed my refund 6 days ago and I still don't see the money.
Card refunds are returned to the original payment method and take 5 to 10 business days to appear, depending on your bank. We issued yours on the 13th, so the outer edge would be the 27th.
Can you send it to a different card? That one is expiring.
No — refunds must go back to the original payment method. If the card is closed entirely the bank returns the funds to us and we then arrange a bank transfer, which adds another cycle.

resolution: Card refunds take 5-10 business days to the original payment method. Cannot be redirected to a different card.

subject: Refund by bank transfer timeline

conversation.text: We paid by invoice and bank transfer, not card. How long does a refund take?
Bank transfer refunds are slower than card. Allow 15 business days from approval. We need the IBAN and account holder name in writing from a billing contact on the account before we can start.

resolution: Bank transfer refunds take 15 business days and require written IBAN confirmation from an authorised billing contact.

subject: VAT number missing from my invoice

conversation.text: Our finance team rejected the invoice because it has no VAT ID on it. Can you reissue it?

A VAT ID has to be on the account before the invoice is generated. We cannot add it retroactively to an already-issued invoice — the document is immutable once issued for audit reasons. Add the VAT ID under Billing > Tax Details and every future invoice will carry it.
So this invoice is stuck without VAT?
For this one we can issue a credit note against it and raise a fresh invoice with the VAT ID present. That is the supported path.

resolution: VAT IDs cannot be added retroactively to issued invoices. Workaround is a credit note plus a reissued invoice.

subject: Charged twice this month

conversation.text: There are two identical charges on the 1st for the same amount.

I see a failed charge that was retried. When a payment fails we retry on day 1, day 3 and day 7. Occasionally the first attempt settles late at the bank and both land. The duplicate is automatically detected and voided within 48 hours.
It's been 4 days.
Then it settled rather than pending, so auto-void did not apply. I have refunded the duplicate manually — 5 to 10 business days back to the card.

resolution: Duplicate charge from failed-payment retry schedule (day 1, 3, 7). Refunded manually.

subject: Proration when adding seats mid-cycle

conversation.text: If I add 5 seats halfway through the month, do I pay full price for them?
No. Added seats are prorated to the day for the remainder of the billing period, charged immediately as a one-off adjustment. Your next full invoice then includes all seats at the normal rate.
And if I remove seats?
Removals are not prorated. Removed seats stay billed until the end of the current period, then drop off the next invoice. You keep access to them until then.

resolution: Seat additions are prorated daily and charged immediately. Seat removals are not prorated and take effect at the next billing period.

subject: Getting 401 with a key I just created

conversation.text: Brand new key, immediately 401 Unauthorized.

Two usual causes. First, new keys take up to 60 seconds to propagate across our edge nodes. Second, the header must be Authorization: Bearer sk_live_... — we see a lot of people send the raw key with no Bearer prefix, which returns 401 rather than 400.
It was the Bearer prefix. What's the difference between sk_live and sk_test?
sk_test keys only reach the sandbox and never touch production data or real billing. They are also exempt from rate limits.

resolution: 401 caused by missing Bearer prefix. Also noted 60s key propagation delay and sk_test vs sk_live distinction.

subject: Webhook endpoint missed several events

conversation.text: Our endpoint was down for maintenance for about two hours and we think we lost events.

You very likely did not lose them. We retry failed deliveries 5 times over 24 hours with exponential backoff — roughly at 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours and 12 hours after the first failure. Anything still failing after the 5th attempt is marked permanently failed.
How do I get the permanently failed ones?
The Events page keeps 30 days of history and has a Replay button, individually or in bulk by time range.

resolution: Webhooks retry 5 times over 24 hours with exponential backoff. Permanently failed events can be replayed from 30 days of Events history.

subject: How do I verify webhook signatures?

conversation.text: We want to confirm webhook payloads actually come from you.

Every delivery carries an X-SoftSDK-Signature header: an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body using your endpoint's signing secret. Compute it over the raw bytes before any JSON parsing — parsing and re-serialising changes whitespace and the signature will not match.
Does the secret rotate?
Only when you rotate it. During rotation we sign with both old and new secrets for 24 hours, so accept either during that window.

resolution: Webhook signature is HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body using the endpoint signing secret, sent in X-SoftSDK-Signature. Dual-signed for 24h during rotation.

subject: Offset pagination returns 400

conversation.text: Passing ?page=2&offset=50 gives me a 400.

Offset pagination is not supported — page and offset are rejected with 400 by design. Use cursor pagination: pass limit (1 to 100, default 25) and the opaque cursor from the previous response's next_cursor field.
How do I know when I'm done?
When next_cursor comes back null, you have reached the last page.

resolution: Offset pagination is unsupported and returns 400. Cursor pagination with limit and next_cursor is the supported approach.

subject: Can I build my own cursor string?

conversation.text: We'd like to jump to an arbitrary point by constructing the cursor ourselves.

Not supported. The cursor is opaque and encodes both the last id and the sort direction. Hand-built cursors will be rejected or silently return wrong pages. Results are ordered by created_at descending unless you pass order=asc, and the cursor is only valid for the direction it was issued for.

resolution: Cursors are opaque and must not be constructed manually. They encode last id plus sort direction.

subject: Password reset link says expired

conversation.text: I clicked the reset link this morning and it says expired. I only requested it last night.
Password reset links are valid for 60 minutes from the moment they are sent. Overnight is well past that. Request a fresh one and use it straight away.
Does requesting a new one kill the old link?
Yes. Only the most recent reset link is valid — issuing a new one immediately invalidates all previous links.

resolution: Password reset links expire after 60 minutes and requesting a new link invalidates all previous ones.

subject: Lost my phone, locked out of MFA

conversation.text: New phone, authenticator app is gone, I can't log in.
Use one of your backup codes. We issue 10 single-use backup codes when MFA is first enabled. Each works exactly once.
I never saved them.

Then an account admin can reset MFA for you from Team > Members. If you are the only admin, we require identity verification and a 24 hour cooling-off period before support can reset it — that delay is deliberate and cannot be waived.

resolution: MFA recovery uses one of 10 single-use backup codes. Admin reset available, or support reset after identity verification and a mandatory 24h cooling-off period.

subject: SAML SSO setup failing at metadata step

conversation.text: Uploading our Okta metadata XML throws 'invalid entity descriptor'.

We support SAML 2.0 only — not WS-Federation and not SAML 1.1. That error usually means the XML is an IdP-initiated bundle rather than the plain IdP metadata descriptor. Export the raw IdP metadata from Okta and upload that.
Does SSO come with automatic user provisioning?

SCIM provisioning is Enterprise-only and configured separately from SSO. SSO alone authenticates existing users; it does not create them. With SSO but no SCIM, users are created on first successful login (just-in-time provisioning) with the default role.

resolution: SAML 2.0 only. SCIM provisioning is Enterprise-only and separate from SSO; without it users are created just-in-time on first login.

subject: Enforce SSO for everyone in the org

conversation.text: Some staff still log in with email and password. We want SSO only.

Turn on Require SSO under Security Settings. It forces every member through the IdP and disables password login. One exception is kept deliberately: the account owner retains password access as a break-glass path so a broken IdP cannot lock the whole org out.

resolution: Require SSO disables password login for all members except the account owner, who keeps break-glass password access.

subject: Delete all our data under GDPR

conversation.text: We are leaving and need a formal confirmation that our data is erased.

On account closure, production data is purged within 30 days. Encrypted backups roll off on a further 90 day cycle, so full erasure across all systems completes within 120 days. We issue a written deletion certificate once the backup cycle completes.
Can you make it faster?
The 30 day production purge can be triggered immediately on request. The 90 day backup cycle is fixed by our retention architecture and cannot be shortened.

resolution: Production data purged within 30 days of closure; backups within a further 90 days for 120 days total. Deletion certificate issued at completion.

subject: Slack integration won't connect

conversation.text: Clicking Connect to Slack sends me back with 'installation failed'.

Installing the SoftSDK Slack app requires Slack workspace admin rights. If you are a regular member, Slack blocks the install and hands back a generic failure. Ask a workspace admin to install it once — after that any member can link their own account.
Which channels can it post to?
Public channels by default. For private channels you must explicitly invite the SoftSDK bot to each one; it cannot discover private channels on its own.

resolution: Slack app install requires workspace admin rights. Bot must be invited manually to private channels.

subject: Salesforce sync dropping records

conversation.text: Roughly 3% of contacts never make it into Salesforce.

The most common cause is Salesforce validation rules rejecting records that pass our own validation — a required custom field on your side that we do not populate. Failed syncs appear under Integrations > Salesforce > Sync Errors with the raw Salesforce error attached.
Sync Errors shows STRING_TOO_LONG on Description.
That confirms it. Salesforce caps Description at 32000 characters and truncation is not automatic. We are treating the lack of truncation as a bug on our side.

resolution: Pending fix. Sync failures caused by Salesforce field limits (Description 32000 chars); errors surface under Sync Errors.

subject: Zapier trigger fires twice

conversation.text: My Zap runs twice for every new record.

Zapier polls every 5 minutes on free Zapier plans and deduplicates on record id. Duplicates almost always mean the id changes between polls — typically because the Zap is watching an updated_at-based trigger rather than a created_at one.
Switched to the New Record trigger and it stopped.
That is the expected fix. Use New Record for creation events and Updated Record only when you genuinely want every edit.

resolution: Duplicate Zap runs caused by using an update-based trigger. Switching to New Record trigger resolved it.

subject: Mobile app crashes on launch after update

conversation.text: iOS app crashes instantly since version 4.2.0. iPhone 13, iOS 18.

4.2.0 shipped a corrupt migration for local cache databases written by 3.x. Deleting and reinstalling the app clears the local cache and resolves it — your data is server-side so nothing is lost except offline cache.
Reinstall fixed it. Will this recur?
No. 4.2.1 detects the bad cache and rebuilds it silently instead of crashing.

resolution: Crash caused by corrupt cache migration in 4.2.0. Fixed by reinstall; permanently fixed in 4.2.1.

subject: How long does offline mode keep working?

conversation.text: Our field engineers lose signal for days. How long can they keep using the app?
Offline mode caches 7 days of records locally. Beyond 7 days the cache is considered stale and the app requires a sync before it will show data again.
What about edits made offline?

Edits queue locally with no time limit and replay on next connection. Conflicts resolve last-write-wins based on the server's receipt time, not the device clock — device clocks drift and we do not trust them.

resolution: Offline cache holds 7 days of records. Offline edits queue indefinitely and resolve last-write-wins on server receipt time.

subject: Push notifications not arriving on Android

conversation.text: Half our Android users get no push notifications.

Aggressive battery optimisation on Samsung, Xiaomi and OnePlus devices is the usual cause — the OS suspends background delivery. The app must be excluded from battery optimisation in system settings; we cannot do that programmatically.
Any way to detect it?
Settings > Notifications inside the app shows a Delivery Health banner when it detects the app is being throttled.

resolution: Android push failures caused by OEM battery optimisation. Users must exclude the app manually; Delivery Health banner surfaces the problem.

subject: Sandbox data appearing in production reports

conversation.text: Test records are showing up in our production dashboard.
That should be impossible — sk_test keys write only to sandbox and sandbox data never surfaces in production reporting. Can you confirm which key the ingestion job uses?
It's using sk_live in staging. That's our mistake.
That explains it. Staging pointed at live. Sandbox data is fully isolated and purged every 30 days, so nothing needs cleaning up on our side — but you will want to delete those live records.

resolution: Not a product defect. Customer's staging environment used a live key. Sandbox data is isolated and purged every 30 days.

subject: Which SDK versions are still supported?

conversation.text: We're pinned to Python SDK 2.4. Should we upgrade?

We support the current major version and the one before it. With 4.x current, 3.x gets security fixes only and 2.x is end of life — no fixes at all. 2.4 will keep working against the API but is unsupported.
When does 3.x go end of life?
12 months after 4.0 shipped, which puts it at March 2027. We announce deprecations at least 6 months ahead on the changelog and by email to account owners.

resolution: Support covers current major plus one previous. 2.x is EOL, 3.x security-only until March 2027. Deprecations announced 6 months ahead.

subject: Request timing out on large exports

conversation.text: Exporting a large date range times out after about 30 seconds.

Synchronous requests are capped at a 30 second gateway timeout and that is not configurable. For large exports use the async export endpoint: POST /v1/exports returns a job id immediately, then poll GET /v1/exports/{id} or receive an export.completed webhook.
How long are export files available?
Download URLs are pre-signed and expire after 24 hours. You can regenerate a fresh URL from the same job id for up to 7 days.

resolution: 30 second gateway timeout is fixed. Large exports must use the async export endpoint; download URLs expire after 24h, regenerable for 7 days.

subject: Can we get a sandbox that mirrors production data?

conversation.text: We'd like our sandbox seeded with a copy of production.

We do not offer production-to-sandbox cloning. It would copy real customer PII into a less restricted environment, which our data policy prohibits. You can seed sandbox through the normal API with synthetic data, and we publish a seed script that generates a representative dataset.

resolution: Production-to-sandbox cloning is not offered due to PII policy. Synthetic seeding via API is the supported alternative.

subject: Invoice sent to wrong email address

conversation.text: Invoices go to a person who left the company.

Invoices go to the billing contact, which is separate from the account owner and from team member emails. Change it under Billing > Contacts. You can set multiple billing contacts and all of them receive every invoice.
Can I get the last 6 months resent to the new address?
Yes — all past invoices are downloadable any time from Billing > History, and I have emailed the last 6 months to the new contact.

resolution: Billing contact is separate from account owner. Multiple contacts supported; past invoices available under Billing > History.

subject: Downgrade from Enterprise to Pro mid-contract

conversation.text: We want to move down to Pro next month.
Enterprise agreements are annual, so a downgrade takes effect at the contract renewal date rather than immediately, and the remaining term is not refundable. Your renewal is 2026-11-30.
What do we lose on Pro?
SCIM provisioning, the 6000 req/min rate limit drops to 600, audit log retention falls from 2 years to 90 days, and you move from a named CSM to standard support.

resolution: Enterprise downgrades take effect at annual renewal, not immediately. Documented feature deltas between Enterprise and Pro.

subject: Audit log retention period

conversation.text: Our auditors want 2 years of access logs. Do you keep them?
Enterprise retains audit logs for 2 years. Pro retains 90 days and Free does not include audit logs at all. Export is available as CSV or via the audit API.
Can we stream them into our SIEM?
Yes, on Enterprise. We support streaming to S3 and to Splunk HEC. There is no native Datadog destination — customers usually route via S3.

resolution: Audit retention: Enterprise 2 years, Pro 90 days, Free none. SIEM streaming to S3 and Splunk HEC on Enterprise.

subject: Failed payment — when do you suspend the account?

conversation.text: Our card expired and payment failed. How long before you cut us off?
We retry on day 1, day 3 and day 7. If all three fail the account moves to a grace period on day 8, which is read-only for API access but keeps the dashboard usable. Full suspension is day 14.
Is anything deleted at suspension?
No. Suspension blocks access but deletes nothing. Data is retained for 60 days after suspension, and paying the outstanding invoice restores access immediately.

resolution: Dunning: retries on days 1/3/7, read-only grace on day 8, suspension day 14. No data deleted; 60 day retention after suspension.

subject: Do you support IP allowlisting?

conversation.text: Security team wants API access restricted to our office IPs.

IP allowlisting is available on Enterprise, configured per API key rather than per account, so you can lock a production key to your egress ranges while leaving a development key open. IPv4 and IPv6 CIDR ranges are both accepted.
What happens to a blocked request?
403 Forbidden with an ip_not_allowed error code, and the attempt is recorded in the audit log.

resolution: IP allowlisting is Enterprise-only, configured per API key, supports IPv4/IPv6 CIDR. Blocked requests return 403 ip_not_allowed.

subject: Exporting data before we cancel

conversation.text: We're cancelling. How do we get all our data out?
Settings > Data Export produces a full account export as newline-delimited JSON plus any uploaded files. Large accounts take a few hours and you get an email when it is ready.
Can we still export after cancelling?
Yes, for 30 days after closure while the account is in the pending-purge window. After the 30 day production purge the export tool no longer has anything to read.

resolution: Full export as NDJSON plus files from Settings > Data Export. Remains available for 30 days after account closure.

subject: Rate limit headers missing from responses

conversation.text: I don't see any rate limit headers on my responses.
They are present on every response except 5xx errors. You should see X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset, where Reset is a Unix timestamp for the start of the next window.
Found them — our HTTP client was lowercasing and I was matching case-sensitively.
Common one. HTTP header names are case-insensitive by spec, so always match case-insensitively.

resolution: Rate limit headers X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset are present on all non-5xx responses. Customer issue was case-sensitive header matching.

subject: Can we self-host SoftSDK?

conversation.text: Our procurement is asking whether an on-premise install is possible.

SoftSDK is cloud-only and we do not offer an on-premise or single-tenant install. For data residency requirements we can pin your account to the EU or US region, chosen at account creation and not changeable afterwards without a full migration.

resolution: No on-premise offering. Data residency handled via EU/US region pinning set at account creation.
